Reading list

The IT industry is changing before our very eyes. With AI entering the software architecture and development landscape, whether we like it or not, we are set to be taken on a roller coaster, the likes of which we haven’t seen since the advent of microservices and cloud-native computing. If the last decade was spent mostly on mastering and optimizing the cloud and micro- or nano-scale service-oriented architecture, the next decade will likely be spent figuring out how to master AI for building a new generation of IT systems.

These new systems will harness the power of AI in ways that, even today, are perhaps not fully comprehensible, as this space is moving forward at a neck-breaking pace, and last year’s best practice is this year’s antipattern. This rapid pace of innovation comes with many challenges, but can also be exciting for those willing to join the ride.

In this series, we try to establish agentic AI architecture as a new type of software architecture that will likely dominate the industry for years to come. The articles, written by industry experts, cover various elements and aspects of agentic AI architecture. We aim to present the latest trends and developments shaping the new type of architecture as it enters the mainstream.

While it’s impossible to characterize the new type of software architecture fully at this point, we hope this series offers useful insights into how the agentic AI space will shape the future of the IT industry in the coming years. Agentic AI Architecture is still in its infancy, but we hope to track how it evolves and matures and cover all key milestones and breakthroughs in the future.

You can download the entire series collated in PDF format, in the associated eMag.

 

Series Contents

1

From Microservice to Agents: The Next Evolution of Distributed Systems

This article discusses the shift in distributed systems architecture, driven by large language models (LLMs) and reasoning systems. Mallika Rao argues that agentic AI architectures focus on decomposing decisions, much like microservice architectures decompose functionality. Additionally, the author shares initial architectural patterns and failure modes introduced by the new paradigm, highlighting the increased importance of observability and reliability in these new types of agentic systems.

Article by: Mallika Rao

2

The Evolution of Agentic Harnesses: From Chains to Graph to Code

Karthik Ramgopal describes how building agents that interact with large language models has evolved in recent years from ad hoc experiments to resilient, production-grade architectures. Karthik also shares best practices and battle-tested advice for robust agentic AI architectures, drawn from his experience building several agentic solutions.  

Article by: Karthik Ramgopal

To be released: Week of Oct 26, 2026

3

Systemic Approach to Memory, Knowledge, and Context in the Agentic AI Architectures

Adi Polak delves into the knowledge layer of agentic AI and introduces context engineering as a new discipline that has emerged in the agentic AI space. Adi argues that context management should be tuned to the system it supports and discusses key elements and mechanisms for incorporating high-quality context data into LLM prompts to reduce or eliminate hallucinations.

Article by: Adi Polak

To be released: Week of Nov 02, 2026

4

Agentic AI Architecture Framework for Enterprises

In this article, Subash Natarajan and Ahilan Ponnusamy describe a three-tier framework for designing and delivering agentic AI systems, covering many distinct elements, solutions, and patterns. The authors then offer industry-specific examples and share implementation strategies and guiding principles required for successful adoption.

Article by: Subash Natarajan and Ahilan Ponnusamy

5

Agentic AI Architecture: Current Challenges and Future Opportunities

Finally, Rafał Gancarz wraps up the eMag's overarching topic by examining how agentic AI architecture, as a new generation of software architecture, will change the IT industry as we know it today. Rafał connects the dots and covers a broad range of areas and architectural aspects that will need to adapt to address the challenges posed by agentic AI.

Article by: Rafał Gancarz

To be released: Week of Nov 09, 2026

About the Author

Rafał Gancarz

Rafał is an experienced technology leader and expert. He's currently helping Starbucks make its Commerce Platform scalable, resilient, and cost-effective. Previously, Rafał has been involved in designing and building large-scale, distributed, and cloud-based systems for Cisco, Accenture, Capita, ICE, Callsign, and others. His interests span architecture & design, continuous delivery, observability, and operability, as well as sociotechnical and organizational aspects of software delivery.
